questions.question: What does the financial term "cheapflation" refer to?
options: Premium luxury goods increasing in price faster than budget items
Low-cost and budget-friendly goods rising in price at a faster rate than premium alternatives
Companies shrinking product package sizes while keeping retail prices the same
A decline in overall inflation caused by an oversupply of cheap imported products
questions.explanation: Cheapflation occurs when budget-friendly staple items experience higher percentage price increases than luxury options. Today's story highlights how this trend disproportionately burdens lower-income households who rely heavily on low-cost goods.

questions.question: In today's economic reports, what does the 2% figure represent regarding artificial intelligence?
options: The recent drop in U.S. gross domestic product due to international tech tariffs
The expected annual rate of labor productivity growth across all U.S. industries
The estimated share of total U.S. gross domestic product currently generated by the AI sector
The proportion of corporate tech spending dedicated to compliance and data security
questions.explanation: The 2% figure measures artificial intelligence's current contribution to overall U.S. Gross Domestic Product. Today's story explains that such a heavy economic reliance on a single tech sector increases the risk of broader market vulnerability if AI investment slows down.

questions.question: Why does Best Buy's recent strong sales growth matter to economic analysts?
options: It shows that a cyclical replacement wave for older electronics can drive retail growth even when overall spending is constrained
It proves that broader consumer sentiment and disposable income have fully recovered to pre-inflation levels
It signals that brick-and-mortar retail stores are completely immune to supply chain friction and import tariffs
It indicates that consumers are shifting all of their spending away from essential goods to purchase luxury electronics
questions.explanation: Best Buy's sales beat shows how predictable replacement cycles—such as upgrading pandemic-era laptops and TVs—can sustain business revenue during tough economic periods. It demonstrates that product lifespans can create growth opportunities even when inflation pressures everyday household budgets.
